frequency_question: How often do targeted voting bills that reach serious floor consideration successfully pass the U.S. Senate within the given timeframe and meet all specific documentary requirements of the text?
membership_rule: Includes major standalone federal voter eligibility bills or identical successor bills introduced and voted on in the U.S. Senate. Excludes general omnibus bills where the specific voter eligibility provision was merely an amendment without standalone text matching the successor criteria.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 1 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 1 named major iteration; the SAVE Act framework represents a distinct legislative vehicle category.
known_gaps: Limited direct historical analogues for exact strict documentary citizenship verification bills brought to standalone Senate votes under current filibuster rules.
skeleton: Legislative sessions with polarized Senate control considering restrictive federal election integrity bills requiring documentary proof of citizenship.
multiplier: 1 observed case / 1 relevant benchmark case matching exact text and Senate procedural hurdle environment
validity_reason: Valid through the duration of the current congressional composition and Senate rules environment.
